notes: Unplugged day. Students find a policy or law at an earlier point on the timeline and what it did to the technology it touched, reading two views and a dated source for it. Depth: cause and effect of a rule at a first look, no legal detail and no reading of statutes; the full proposal skill is owned in grade 11 (g11-policy-change). Paper only: case cards and the class timeline. Model carried: timeline. Case: the 1998 federal children's online privacy law, from the Federal Trade Commission's rule page, checked there when the unit is written.

words: scatter; multivariate; variable; chart; color; size; pattern; trend
notes: Device day. Students plot three variables in one chart (x, y and color) from a given table and say what pattern they see and what the chart cannot show. Depth: reading and making a three-variable chart with a visible trend, no statistics beyond that; the full skill is owned in grade 11 (g11-multivariate-viz). Paper path: the same points plotted by hand on printed squares with colored pencils. Model carried: data-visualization.

words: skill; career; certificate; training; project; portfolio; choose
notes: Unplugged day, a short portfolio session. Students list the skills in the work they have built so far (reading code, testing, explaining, working in a pair), match each to two kinds of job and name one skill to build next. Depth: naming and matching skills; certificates and pathways are left for g12-career-goals. Paper list, kept private by default. Owned in grade 12.

words: source; quality; representative; bias; privacy; sample; label; balance
notes: Unplugged and device day. A given training set is checked for where it came from, how clean it is, who is missing, who might be harmed and what personal information it holds. Students write a data review before the model is built in g11-build-ml-model. In-grade order for grade 11: this row before g11-build-ml-model, which builds on the data review written here. Specialty I addition (S1-AIN-DD-02): after the review, students change the training set (add, remove or rebalance examples) and show with the same test-table whether fairness and accuracy of the output improved or worsened.

words: train; test; accuracy; model; overfit; split; label; evaluate; claim; metric
notes: Device day. Students build a small model for a chosen task from a supplied dataset using a browser tool, split the data into training and test, and report accuracy and where it fails. Part met without a device: a pretend model on cards, marked part met without a device. After g11-training-data-review. Closing session: students test one claim about their model (for example, it is right nine times in ten) against the test-table and a metric, using the test-case habit of g10-evaluate-algorithms, which is used on a model here. The steps of the build (choose data, split, train, test, report) are first written as pseudocode lines, so the model chain keeps pseudocode in use through grade 11.

words: ethical; societal; bias; rule-based; data-driven; audit; evidence; harm
notes: Unplugged day. A rule-based and a data-driven algorithm for the same job (sorting applications, say) are audited for ethical, societal and bias effects with evidence, giving two views and a dated source for each. Students name who is helped, who is harmed and what the audit could not see, and recommend how each algorithm could be refined. Left out: building either algorithm. Paper path: written outputs for the same ten cases printed side by side. Model carried: benefit-risk-chart.

words: multivariate; classify; predict; chart; relationship; variable; dataset; claim
notes: Device day. With a chart tool, no text code, students build a visualization of a dataset with several variables to answer a question or make a classification or prediction. Part met without a device: hand-drawn plots on printed data, marked part met without a device. Specialty I addition (S1-DSC-VZ-11): students compare an honest chart with one that breaks a graphical convention (a cut axis, a crowded scale) and say what each convention protects the reader from, then redraw the broken chart correctly.

words: simulation; limit; decision; assumption; evaluate; visualization; model; uncertainty
notes: Device and unplugged day. Students judge a given simulation or chart for whether it answers the question, what decision it supports and what it cannot show.

words: specification; correct; effective; user experience; value; requirement; test; responsible
notes: Device day. A program is checked against a written specification: does it do what was asked, does it work well for the users, does it respect the values the team set (privacy, access). Specialty I addition (S1-SWD-TR-07): students write a test plan for the program before running it, with ordinary inputs, edge cases, error cases and unusual user inputs, and the plan is the test-table used for the check. The test plan has cases for each function alone and for the parts together, on a program with several functions and a list, and some cases come from a supplied saved list of generated test suggestions that students judge before use.

words: reliability; accuracy; generated; requirement; review; test; flaw; ownership
notes: Supplied saved code samples, some right and some flawed, for a given requirement. Students test each against the requirement with edge cases (an empty list, one item, repeated values) and judge it for accuracy, reliability and fit to the requirement, and name the flaw. No student uses a live tool. Each sample also gets an ownership note (who wrote it, what credit it needs), the next look at HS-PRO-PD-14 after g10-apis-docs before g12-attribution owns it.

words: concept; solution; real-world; benefit; harm; design; emerging; human; intelligence
notes: Unplugged day. Students sketch a conceptual solution to a real local problem with an emerging technology and analyze its benefits and harms, with two views and a dated source for the main claim. Depth: a sketch and an argument, no working prototype. The question of human and artificial intelligence is raised here for debate in grade 12 (g12-human-vs-ai). Paper path: a sketch and a benefit-risk-chart. Model carried: benefit-risk-chart.

words: legislation; policy; propose; modify; ethical innovation; risk; stakeholder
notes: Unplugged day. Students propose a change to an existing policy that encourages innovation and cuts risk, defend it with evidence and name who is affected, using two views and a dated source for the existing policy. Depth: a one-page proposal, no legal drafting. Placed with g11-infrastructure-impact in the year. Paper path: a written proposal and a timeline of the policy. Models carried: timeline, benefit-risk-chart. Cases are from memory, to be checked before use.

words: flaw; patch; fix; test; toy system; design; vulnerability; solution
notes: Device day on a toy system built into the page. Students find a flaw in a supplied system (a weak password rule, an open page), write a fix and test it. No real system is probed. Paper path: a printed toy system with a written flaw, a written fix and a written test of it; met in full on paper, since the standard asks for a reasoned, high-level solution to a simulated or described flaw. The fix is a setting change or a rule, never code or an implementation. Specialty I addition (S1-CYB-TS-08): the flaw is rated on the cia-triangle, naming which of confidentiality, integrity and availability it breaks, the state the data is in and the kind of control the fix is. The fix names a technical step and a non-technical one (a rule or training) and the consequences if the flaw stays. Two common threats (a program that locks files for ransom, a flood of requests that takes a service down) are rated the same way.

words: infrastructure; society; environment; who affected; energy; data center; access
notes: Unplugged day. Students trace how a computing system and its infrastructure (cables, data centers, power, repair) affect society and the environment and who is affected and why, using a local case with two views and a dated source. Depth: a traced chain of effects, no engineering detail. Paper path: a system-diagram drawn on a printed map. Models carried: system-diagram, network-diagram. g8-design-for-all returns here after a skip of grades 9 and 10: who can and cannot use a system (access and design for different users) becomes who a whole infrastructure serves and who it leaves out. Cases are from memory, to be checked before use. The chain includes where a device's materials are mined and who builds and recycles it.

words: team; career; skill; role; diverse; project; plan
notes: Unplugged day. A short project plan in which each student takes a role on a team (design, build, test, explain), says what skill that role asks for and how a different perspective on the team would change the plan. This is a role-and-team plan that feeds g12-diverse-teams; the personal career half is moved to g12-career-goals. Depth: roles and perspectives named and used, no hiring or pay. Paper plan, kept private by default. No new model is carried. Owned in grade 12.

words: large scale; environmental; ethical; privacy; AI; society; energy; consent
notes: Unplugged day. Large-scale collection and processing, including data used for AI, is evaluated for society, environmental and ethical effects, with two views and a dated source for each. g9-data-and-people returns here after a skip of grade 10: the first look in grade 9 at who benefits and who is exposed is reopened with the same kind of case at full depth, and the owner skill is the written evaluation. Left out: any law reading, which is g12-data-policy-debate the next year. Paper path: case cards and a benefit-risk-chart. Models carried: data-table, benefit-risk-chart. The cases include data sovereignty and the spread of false information.

words: bias; accuracy; harm; output; evaluate; supplied; check; source
notes: Supplied saved outputs from generated-text and image systems (text answers, code samples and images, printed or on one page), some right and some flawed or biased, so there is no live tool. Students evaluate each for bias, accuracy and harm with evidence, name the first thing that is wrong and say how they would check it against a second source. Depth: judging output, not building or tuning a system. Paper path: the outputs printed with a margin for notes. Model carried: test-table. Specialty I addition (S1-AIN-HR-09): beyond judging single outputs, students name the limits and likely biases of the kind of system that produced them and where in its design or data each comes from. For S1-AIN-HR-09 students also count errors by group for the class model from g11-build-ml-model (or, for a class with no grade 11 model, a supplied saved model with its test-table) and for a supplied set of saved outputs from a system others made, and compare the gaps.

words: value; embedded; design; choice; stakeholder; algorithm; trade-off; priority
notes: Unplugged day. Students trace the values built into an algorithmic system (what it counts, what it ignores, who it asks) from a supplied description and write one paragraph that states those values and one that they would change, with two views. Depth: tracing and articulating values, no redesign of code. Paper path only. Model carried: benefit-risk-chart.

words: policy; regulation; responsible use; debate; efficacy; evidence; law; claim
notes: Unplugged day. A structured debate on how well a data policy or regulation (a rule on consent, on retention, on sharing) works to keep data use responsible, with two prepared sides and dated sources. Students judge efficacy against the evidence, not against their side. The written preparation can serve the ELA seminar. Paper path: prepared cards and a scoring sheet. Model carried: benefit-risk-chart. Cases are from memory, to be checked before use. Specialty I addition (S1-DSC-PP-13): the debate cases include how collecting and using data affects groups that are under-represented or marginalized, with evidence for each effect named. The debate also weighs social approaches (a public campaign, people changing their own habits) beside the rule, and the Specialty I cases end with one way to collect a fairer dataset.

words: workflow; design document; role; task; review; version; branch; team
notes: Device day, several weeks. A team builds one program with a design document, a task list that splits the weeks (plan and design, build in pairs, a review step, a final check) and clear task roles. In the review step a teammate reads the code against the design document and a test-table and either signs off or returns it. Each member's part and contribution is recorded in a log. Depth: a working method for a four-person team, no version-control tool required. Paper path: the design document and the log kept on paper with code printed for review. Model carried: text-program, test-table. Specialty I addition (S1-SWD-PP-08): the design document records whose needs and views shaped each decision, and the review step asks whether the program reflects more than the team's own view. Version control (S1-SWD-PP-08): part met until our editor's offline version history with branch, review and merge exists; then the review step uses it (Cory, 2026-11-21, Desk q-fix-cs-2).

words: feedback; refine; testing results; user; impact; effective; iterate; value
notes: Device day. The team program is tried by two users outside the team, who say what they see and what confuses them; the team records testing results, changes one thing at a time and re-checks the program against the values it set in the design document. Depth: two rounds of feedback, no survey. Paper path: the program printed and walked through by a user with the team taking notes. Model carried: test-table. Specialty I addition (S1-SWD-UX-05): the team states the intended users and setting first and judges each change by how well it serves them, using a short human-centered design cycle. For S1-SWD-UX-05 the team also runs a heuristic review against a short list (usable, consistent, accessible, user in control), asking how the program serves users of different abilities, languages and cultures.

words: attribution; license; intellectual property; credit; permission; cite; generated; ownership
notes: Unplugged day. Students apply attribution to their team program: each library, each piece of other people's code, any generated code and each image, sound or other media asset gets a credit line and a note on what permission it needs, from the license terms the class was given. Depth: credit and permission in plain terms, no legal reading. Builds on the first looks in g10-apis-docs and g11-evaluate-generated-code. Paper path: the credit lines written on the printed program. Model carried: text-program.

words: diverse; team; perspective; computational thinking; project; role; solve
notes: Unplugged day. A diverse team on the project is studied for how different perspectives improved the design, using a log from g12-team-workflow, which runs earlier in the grade. Students pick two moments in the log where a different view changed a decision and say what the team would have lost without it. Depth: evidence from the log, not opinion about people. Paper path: the log read in pairs. Model carried: benefit-risk-chart. Students also read two supplied published accounts by computing professionals from different backgrounds (sources in the teacher line, no company names) and say how each used computational thinking and met a barrier at work and opened the field to others.

words: career; goal; skill; portfolio; pathway; plan; field
notes: Unplugged day. Students connect what they learned to a personal goal and write a plan: the goal, two skills they have shown in the course (evidence from their portfolio), one pathway to check, after researching two computing-related fields from supplied field cards (duties only) and one next step. Depth: a plan, no comparison of schools or pay. Shared at the level of ideas, not personal details; kept private by default. Paper plan. No new model is carried.

words: consciousness; intelligence; ethics; responsibility; debate; human; artificial
notes: Unplugged day. A structured debate on how human and artificial intelligence differ and what that means for ethics and who is responsible, with two views and dated sources. Students argue the side they are given, then write which point moved them. Depth: reasoned argument from cases already met, no claims about machine minds. Paper path: prepared cards and a scoring sheet. The written part can serve the ELA seminar. Model carried: benefit-risk-chart.

words: law; policy; rationale; design; use; rule; regulate; evaluate
notes: Unplugged day. A law or policy that governs how computing systems are designed or used (a rule on data protection, on access for people with disabilities, on copying) is evaluated for its reason, its effects and its gaps, with two views and a dated source. Depth: reading a short plain-language summary, no statute text. Paper path: summary cards and a benefit-risk-chart. Cases are from memory, to be checked before use. Technical, legal and social approaches (a design rule, a law, a public campaign) are compared for the same problem.

words: capstone; design; module; data structure; plan; build; present; review
notes: Device day, several weeks. The team program of g12-team-workflow is built from a design in pseudocode and a flowchart, with modules and a data structure, and presented with a trace of the key part. Owned earlier; here used at full size. HS-DAT-IM-27 moved to grade 11 so the capstone year owns 10 ids (Cory, 2026-11-20).
